periods.analysis: At 16% complete and green, the Regional Pandemic Preparedness Initiative is where I would expect it to be for an early build: foundational agreements are done, not merely discussed. The Regional MOU is complete, 200 days past its dueOffsetDays marker, and the stockpile & logistics plan is complete, 60 days past its dueOffsetDays marker, giving Harborview and our county partners a shared operating frame before the next respiratory season. The multi-agency response exercise is in-progress with a 15-day dueOffsetDays marker, and the after-action improvements remain not-started with a 110-day dueOffsetDays marker, which is appropriate because we should not prescribe fixes before we test the system. The practical work this quarter centered on mapping PPE caches at Fire Station 4, the North Pier clinic pod, and the Seabright Community Center dispensing site.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green trajectory by locking the completed MOU and logistics plan into department operating procedures, not just project files. Extend the exercise planning to include two vulnerable-population routes: assisted living facilities along Bayview Drive and the commuter workforce clinics near Harborview Station. I recommend Public Health run a tabletop inject on school absenteeism before the full exercise so prevention decisions are practiced early.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 16% to 23%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7 percentage points, and the initiative remains green. That movement is meaningful because it reflects coordination work that is often invisible until an emergency exposes gaps. The Regional MOU remains complete, the stockpile & logistics plan remains complete, the multi-agency response exercise remains in-progress with the 15-day dueOffsetDays marker, and after-action improvements remain not-started with the 110-day marker. We used the quarter to validate delivery lanes for masks, antivirals, and test kits from the Civic Yard warehouse to the westside clinic corridor and the ferry terminal triage point.
periods.recommendations: Sustain progress by converting the validated delivery lanes into laminated route cards for drivers and alternates. Extend partner readiness by adding Harborview Unified School District nurses and two major employers to the next exercise planning call. I recommend a simple weekly status huddle until the exercise is complete, focused on decisions needed, not general updates.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 23% to 30%, another 7 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, with green status maintained. We are still in the prevention-first phase: clarifying roles, checking inventories, and reducing confusion before residents need services. The Regional MOU and stockpile & logistics plan remain complete, while the multi-agency response exercise remains in-progress and the after-action improvements are correctly still not-started. This quarter’s useful detail was the registration of three dispensing cohorts—healthcare workers, congregate-care residents, and essential municipal crews—so the exercise can test prioritization as well as throughput.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green status by keeping the cohort definitions stable through the exercise; changing them late would create noise rather than insight. Extend the work by adding a pharmacy-vendor contact drill with Seaside Rx and Harborview Medical Supply, including after-hours numbers. I recommend that the exercise controller team track time-to-decision for each cohort, because speed and equity both matter in a public health emergency.

periods.analysis: Completion increased from 30% to 37%, a 7 percentage point quarter-over-quarter movement, and the initiative remains green. The pace is steady and appropriate for a regional preparedness effort, especially in a fast-growing city where new clinics, schools, and senior housing sites keep changing the response map. The completed Regional MOU and completed stockpile & logistics plan continue to provide the backbone, while the multi-agency response exercise stays in-progress and after-action improvements remain not-started. Staff added the East Harbor urgent care site and the new Mariner’s Landing senior complex to the exercise directory, which improves population coverage without changing the core plan.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by freezing the exercise participant roster two weeks before the drill and requiring each agency to name a primary and backup lead. Extend the plan by testing one coastal disruption scenario, such as fog-related ferry delay or causeway congestion, because Harborview’s geography is part of our risk profile. I recommend preparing an after-action template now so findings can move quickly into improvements once the exercise is complete.

periods.analysis: The initiative moved from 37% to 44%, again a 7 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains green. This is the point in the arc where planning should become muscle memory, and the in-progress multi-agency response exercise is doing that by forcing departments to practice handoffs. The Regional MOU remains complete, the stockpile & logistics plan remains complete, and after-action improvements remain not-started until the exercise produces evidence. We also tested draft public messaging in English, Spanish, Vietnamese, and Tagalog with the Community Health Promoter cohort, which is prevention work because trusted messages reduce delays in care-seeking.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping the multilingual message library under Public Health version control with dates, owners, and approval paths. Extend the exercise to include a rumor-control inject coordinated with the City Manager’s communications team and the 211 regional call center. I recommend tracking which messages residents understand on first read, not just whether the translations are technically accurate.

periods.analysis: Progress rose from 44% to 51%, a 7 percentage point quarter-over-quarter increase, and the initiative remains green. Crossing the halfway mark is important, but I do not read it as permission to relax; preparedness is maintained by repetition and correction. The Regional MOU and stockpile & logistics plan remain complete, the multi-agency response exercise remains in-progress, and after-action improvements remain not-started with the 110-day dueOffsetDays marker. This quarter we reconciled cache counts for N95s, pediatric masks, gloves, and specimen kits at Asset Caches PH-02, PH-05, and PH-07, resolving minor labeling differences before they could become operational delays.
periods.recommendations: Sustain performance by moving cache reconciliation to a monthly cycle during respiratory virus season and a quarterly cycle afterward. Extend readiness by adding barcode scans for PH-02, PH-05, and PH-07 into the emergency logistics dashboard used by Fire and Public Works. I recommend a no-fault discrepancy log so staff report stockpile issues early rather than trying to solve them informally.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 51% to 58%, maintaining the same 7 percentage point quarter-over-quarter movement and green status. The work is now less about creating documents and more about proving that people can use them under pressure. The Regional MOU and stockpile & logistics plan remain complete, the multi-agency response exercise remains in-progress, and the after-action improvements remain not-started because the evidence set is still being built. During the quarter, the exercise team ran a communications check across Public Health, Fire, Harborview Medical Center, and the county emergency operations desk, with particular attention to weekend escalation paths.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green status by repeating the communications check on a Saturday morning and a weekday evening, when staffing patterns are different. Extend the exercise by including behavioral health triage and family reunification messaging, both of which affect community stability during a prolonged emergency. I recommend pre-assigning owners for likely after-action categories—logistics, clinical operations, communications, and equity—so improvements can start promptly when authorized.

periods.analysis: Completion increased from 58% to 65%, another 7 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, and the initiative remains green. Over eight quarters, Harborview has moved from early regional alignment to a more practiced, prevention-oriented emergency readiness system. The Regional MOU remains complete, the stockpile & logistics plan remains complete, the multi-agency response exercise remains in-progress with the 15-day dueOffsetDays marker, and after-action improvements remain not-started with the 110-day marker. The strongest operational sign this quarter was consistent participation from clinics, Fire, school health staff, and community-based partners in the final exercise design sessions, which means the plan is being owned broadly rather than held by one department.
periods.recommendations: Sustain and extend the green trajectory by scheduling the next full exercise window now and protecting staff time on agency calendars. Convert the most stable elements—the MOU contacts, cache routes, cohort definitions, and multilingual messages—into an annual preparedness maintenance packet. I recommend that once the multi-agency response exercise closes, Harborview move immediately into after-action improvements with ranked actions, owners, and 30-, 60-, and 90-day deadlines.

periods.analysis: 90% complete. 3 of 4 milestones are done. Next up: After-action improvements (due Nov 13, 2026).
periods.recommendations: No action needed. Continue on the current plan.
